taxpayer.notes: Unmarried at close of 2015; lived with partner Leonor Madrigal, their daughter Maria Terrones (19), and Ms. Madrigal's two grandchildren J.V. and L.V.; only employed household member; wages $12,893; return prepared by paid preparer.

adjustments: disallowed dependency exemption deductions for Maria Terrones, J.V., and L.V.
changed filing status from head of household to married filing separately and adjusted standard deduction
disallowed earned income credit (Maria Terrones, J.V., L.V.)
imposed sec. 6662(a) penalty (negligence and substantial understatement)

findings_of_fact.fact: Throughout 2015 petitioner lived with partner Leonor Madrigal, their daughter Maria Terrones, and Ms. Madrigal's grandchildren J.V. and L.V. (siblings)
findings_of_fact.snippet: Throughout 2015 petitioner lived with his partner, Leonor Madrigal, their daughter, Maria Terrones, and Ms. Madrigal's two grandchildren, J.V. and L.V.,

findings_of_fact.fact: At close of 2015 neither J.V. nor L.V. had attained age 17; Maria Terrones was 19
findings_of_fact.snippet: As of the close of 2015 neither J.V. nor L.V. had attained age 17, and Maria Terrones was 19 years old.

findings_of_fact.fact: J.V. and L.V. placed in custody of petitioner and Ms. Madrigal by order of District Court of Adams County, Colorado on November 18, 2010 (eligible foster children, sec. 152(f)(1)(C))
findings_of_fact.snippet: By order dated November 18, 2010, the petition for allocation was granted, and petitioner and Ms. Madrigal were awarded custody of J.V. and L.V.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was the only employed household member in 2015; wages $12,893; paid all household expenses
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2015 petitioner was the only employed member of the household. His wages for that year totaled $12,893. He paid all of the household expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner's 2015 AGI as shown on return was $12,893; nothing suggests Ms. Madrigal had income, so petitioner had higher AGI for tiebreaker (sec. 152(c)(4)(A)(ii))
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner's adjusted gross income for 2015 as shown on his return was $12,893.

findings_of_fact.fact: Maria Terrones turned 19 in 2015 and was not shown to be a student (school transcript showed she was not)
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner has not established that Maria Terrones was a student in 2015, and therefore she did not meet the age requirement

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was unmarried at close of 2015 and paid all household expenses of the principal abode for himself, J.V., and L.V.
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner, who was unmarried as of the close of 2015, established that he paid all of the household expenses for the principal abode

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner, unsophisticated in tax matters, relied on a competent paid preparer
findings_of_fact.snippet: He relied upon a competent paid income tax return preparer to: (1) prepare his 2015 Federal income tax return

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to dependency exemption deductions for J.V., L.V., and Maria Terrones for 2015?
issues.holding: Entitled for J.V. and L.V. (eligible foster children; tiebreaker to higher-AGI taxpayer vs. Ms. Madrigal); not for Maria Terrones (age 19, not a student); court made no finding on qualifying-relative status for Maria as it would not affect the deficiency
issues.computable_reason: Relationship (foster child by court order), age, residency, and AGI tiebreaker tests follow mechanically from found facts; Maria's student status is a found fact

issues.question: Does petitioner qualify for head of household filing status for 2015?
issues.holding: Yes; unmarried, maintained (paid all expenses of) home that was principal abode of qualifying children J.V. and L.V. for the year
issues.computable_reason: Follows from marital status, >50% expense payment, and qualifying children found in I1

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to the earned income credit for 2015, and with how many qualifying children?
issues.holding: Entitled to EIC computed with two qualifying children (J.V. and L.V.); Maria Terrones not a qualifying child

amount_determined.description: EIC with two qualifying children, computed under Rule 155

issues.computable_reason: Qualifying-child count from I1; credit from 2015 EIC table given earned income $12,893

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to the child tax credit for J.V. and L.V. for 2015?
issues.holding: Yes; J.V. and L.V. are qualifying children under 17

amount_determined.description: child tax credit for two children, computed under Rule 155

issues.computable_reason: Follows from qualifying-child status and under-17 age at year end

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the sec. 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty for 2015?
issues.holding: Not liable; reasonable cause and good faith (reliance on competent paid preparer)
issues.computable_reason: Decided on reasonable cause/good faith (sec. 6664(c)), a judgment call

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Petitioner allowed dependency exemptions, CTC and EIC for J.V. and L.V. and HOH status; dependency exemption/EIC for Maria Terrones denied; no 6662(a) penalty

notes: Some facts stipulated. Respondent disputed only relationship test for J.V./L.V. and only age test for Maria. Burden on petitioner (sec. 7491(a) not applicable). Ms. Madrigal's AGI not stated; court inferred she had no income. Qualifying-relative status of Maria not decided.
